matt: heads-up — onboarding cassandra-7b (mistral-ish arch). ran the int4 conversion and seeing weird token aliasing / kv-cache collisions on long contexts :thinking_face:
elaine: ugh, can you paste a tiny repro?
matt: minimal repro attached below. note the token ids in the trace repeat and embeddings jump mid-seq:
```
# convert
python -m redwood.tools.convert --model cassandra-7b --out cassandra-7b-int4 --quant int4 --pack-heads
# run
redwood run --model cassandra-7b-int4 --prompt "Paris is the capital of" --max_tokens 20 --debug-token-stream
```
Trace snippet: token_ids: [87, 314, 87, 314, 13]  
Log: embedding[87] changes at step 3 -> cosine to float16 run: 0.985, int4 run: 0.912
elaine: that pattern (87,314,87) screams "token id wrap" or tokenizer remap somewhere in the conversion pipeline. did you use any `--vocab-remap` flag?
matt: no remap. just the default converter. converter log shows `vocab->int` mapping stable, but the runtime kvcache sees shifted indices for some headblocks.
raj: could be head-packing/reshuffle when quantizing. we sometimes reorder head dims for perf (headgroup pack). if pack order != runtime layout, kv offsets look like aliasing. which pack mode did you use?
matt: used `--pack-heads=auto` (default). converter inferred pack to 4-head-chunks.
sophia: also check rotary base / freq table. mismatched rotary_freq_base or embedding projection order can cause token-phase mismatches that look like aliasing for autoregressive models. what are the rotary params in the original vs converted model.json?
matt: original: "rotary_base": 10000, converted model meta says 4096 for some layers. weird.
ben: aha. that's probably the root cause. converter has a fallback for some legacy blocks — if it mis-identifies layer type it sets a default base. that will change the sin/cos align and make kv-cache reuse incorrect across tokens.
elaine: run a quick smoke: compare logits for the same input at layer n (float16 vs int4) and dump rotary phase for a single head. if phases differ by >1e-3, it's the base/freq mismatch.
matt: did that. per-head phase delta ~0.017 radians for head 2 at pos 12. perplexity for small eval set: float16 ppl=2.12, int4 ppl=2.49 (regression). MMLU-ish probe down: 74.3% -> 70.8% (micro-eval).
raj: numbers are material. patch proposal: (1) force converter to copy rotary tables verbatim if present, (2) validate pack-heads layout no-op vs runtime with a checksum, (3) add a tokenizer id shadow-check on convert.
sophia: + add an automated smoke that checks embedding cos similarity for 1k random tokens after conversion. require similarity >= 0.97 for pass.
matt: agree. I'll open a PR for converter guardrails. quick fix local: re-run convert with `--force-rotary-copy` and `--pack-heads=raw`. with that I get ppl=2.16 and cosine=0.973 (much better).
ben: create a follow-up issue to add a CI assert. label: eng-ml/convert.
matt: created issue https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2391 (also pinged @elaine to review).
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout of cassandra-7b-int4 to staging at 2026-03-22T09:00Z (canary: 5%)
elaine: can someone run the tokenizer-normalization sanity? we had weird NFKC vs NFC problems on another model, that could amplify aliasing when indices shift. matt — add the `--tokenizer-normalize nfkc` flag when you re-run.
matt: will do. thanks all. action items: 1) matt: PR for `--force-rotary-copy` + docs; 2) ben: CI assert for pack-layout checksum; 3) sophia: write embedding-sim smoke test; 4) raj: audit pack-heads heuristics. target: block merge until perf smoke green.
sophia: noted. I'll add the smoke test and a tiny eval harness (10 examples) so we fail fast.
ben: thumbs up :+1:
matt: will post updated logs after re-run (ETA ~2h).
